column1: # Species-to-clade table. One row per species that appears as a leaf in a method's trees, or that is a candidate.
# clade is the narrowest of seven nested levels, from outside to inside:
#   outside_vertebrates  no vertebrate whole-genome duplication (invertebrates, tunicates, amphioxus; also plants and fungi)
#   cyclostome           lamprey and hagfish (DISPUTED): they share the first vertebrate round (1R) with the jawed vertebrates;
#                        whether they share the second (2R) is disputed, so treat their position with care
#   gnathostome          jawed vertebrates outside the teleosts: both rounds (1R and 2R). Elephant shark, coelacanth, tetrapods,
#                        and the non-teleost bony fishes (gar, bowfin, reedfish); see the lineage column
#   teleost              Teleostei, but not Percomorpha: both rounds plus the teleost-specific round
#   ovalentaria          Ovalentaria, but not cichlid (includes the sister family Pholidichthyidae)
# Later, lineage-specific duplications (salmonids, carp and goldfish) are not marked: those species are not leaves in the trees.
# lineage is a finer group for the chordates and the non-teleost vertebrates. basis says where each label comes from; 'to confirm'
# rows need the owner. species is the Ensembl-style name (lower case, underscores); names are matched case-insensitively.
